facts.statement: Marta S. Fernández named the genus Mollesaurus in 1999, with Mollesaurus periallus as the type species.
facts.quote: Mollesaurus was named by Marta S. Fernández in 1999 and the type species is Mollesaurus periallus.

facts.statement: Mollesaurus lived during the early Bajocian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 171.6 to 170 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in the Chacaico Sur locality from the Emileia giebeli ammonoid zone of the Los Molles Formation, Cuyo Group, dating to the early Bajocian stage of the Middle Jurassic, about 171.6-170 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Mollesaurus were discovered near the city of Zapala in the Neuquén Basin.
facts.quote: It was found near Zapala city of the Neuquén Basin.

facts.statement: While initially considered a species of Ophthalmosaurus, recent cladistic analyses confirm Mollesaurus is a valid genus of ophthalmosaurid.
facts.quote: Maisch and Matzke (2000) regarded Mollesaurus to be a species of Ophthalmosaurus. However, all recent cladistic analyses found that Mollesaurus is a valid genus of ophthalmosaurid.

facts.statement: Druckenmiller and Maxwell (2010) identified Mollesaurus as the most basal member of the ophthalmosaurid lineage containing Brachypterygius, Caypullisaurus, and Platypterygius, excluding Ophthalmosaurus.
facts.quote: Patrick S. Druckenmiller and Erin E. Maxwell (2010) found it to be the basalmost member of the ophthalmosaurid lineage that included Brachypterygius, Caypullisaurus and Platypterygius (but not Ophthalmosaurus).

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Fischer et al. placed Mollesaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Valentin Fischer, Michael W. Maisch, Darren Naish, Ralf Kosma, Jeff Liston, Ulrich Joger, Fritz J. Krüger, Judith Pardo Pérez, Jessica Tainsh and Robert M. Appleby (2012) found it to be the basalmost member of Ophthalmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Mollesaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Mollesaurus is classified within the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
The time range for Mollesaurus is the Bajocian stage, spanning from 170.9 to 168.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Bajocian (170.9 to 168.6 million years ago)
